title: Architecture & Standards: Unified Guidelines (API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance) + ADR Index
author: Emily Chen
summary: Canonical engineering standards for Redwood Inference covering API design, coding conventions, infrastructure and IaC norms, model-serving requirements, observability metrics/logging/tracing, performance SLOs, and an index of recent ADRs. This doc is the go-to reference for teams implementing services or on-boarding models to production.
body:
Purpose

Provide a single, operationally actionable reference for engineers and product teams building services and model-serving components at Redwood Inference. The goal is consistent quality, observable behavior, predictable performance, and low operational burden.

Scope

Applies to: Redwood-hosted services, Dedicated runtime components, and Private deployment artifacts where engineering teams control code or infra. Does not replace product requirements or customer-specific runbooks.

Principles

- Behavior-first: APIs and services must be instrumented and understandable by default.
- Safe defaults: secure, paginated, and resource-limited patterns by default.
- Observable and debuggable: logs, traces and metrics shipped for every change.
- Small blast radius: feature flags, canaries and rollout policies mandatory for model and infra changes.
- Cost-aware: prefer batch-friendly designs and cache hints when latency SLOs permit.

1) API STANDARDS

Overview
- Use REST (JSON over HTTPS) for public-facing control-plane APIs and gRPC for high-throughput, low-latency internal RPCs.
- All APIs must be versioned in the URL (e.g., /v1/...) and include model/runtime version metadata in responses.

Design rules
- Resource names: use plural nouns (e.g., /models, /deployments).
- HTTP methods: follow RESTful semantics (GET = safe, POST = create/side-effect, PUT = idempotent replace, PATCH = partial update, DELETE = remove).
- Pagination: cursor-based pagination (next_cursor token) for lists > 100 items. Example response snippet:

  {
    "items": [ ... ],
    "next_cursor": "eyJvZmZzZXQiOjEwMH0"
  }

- Error handling: use structured error responses with stable error codes and helpful messages. Schema example:

  {
    "error": {
      "code": "MODEL_NOT_FOUND",
      "message": "Model id m-123 not found",
      "details": {"requested_id": "m-123"}
    }
  }

- Rate limits: return RFC 6585 429 with Retry-After header. Publish per-route limits in the developer console.
- Auth: Bearer tokens via Authorization header. Mutual TLS allowed for private deployments.
- Idempotency: Requests that create resources must accept an Idempotency-Key header to avoid double-creation.
- Field casing: use snake_case for backend services implemented in Python/Go, and camelCase for SDK bindings. API JSON favors snake_case for consistency.

API Lifecycle
1. Design review checklist (pre-PR): schema, versioning impact, quota model, SLO impact, observability knobs.
2. API contract tests added to CI (consumer-driven if available).
3. Deprecation: announce deprecation 90 days prior and provide migration guide.

2) CODING STANDARDS

Languages in scope: Go (backend), Python (inference glue & evals), TypeScript (console & SDKs).

Formatting & linting
- Go: gofmt + golangci-lint with enabled linters: govet, staticcheck, errcheck.
- Python: black, isort, flake8 with max-line-length 100.
- TypeScript: eslint with shared config, prettier for formatting.

Testing
- Unit tests: >= 90% module coverage target for critical services.
- Integration tests: exercised in CI against localstack / test cluster.
- Contract tests: provider and consumer tests for public APIs.

PR & review guidelines
- Max 400 lines of net change per PR except with explicit reviewer approval.
- Every PR must include: summary, testing plan, rollout steps (if infra or model change), and a short risk assessment.
- At least one reviewer from owning team and one from infra/infra-sre for runtime-impacting changes.

Dependency management
- Use renovate for automated dependency updates. Major upgrades require ADR or release notes.

3) INFRASTRUCTURE STANDARDS (IaC & Runtime)

Terraform conventions
- Root modules per product area (e.g., shared-networking, serving-runtime, dedciated-pool).
- Module inputs/outputs must be documented in README.md.
- State: remote backend in Terraform Cloud (or equivalent) with workspace per environment (dev/qa/prod).

Naming & tagging
- Resource names: <team>-<service>-<env>-<component> (e.g., infra-serving-prod-gpupool).
- Tags: owner, cost_center, environment, sla_tier, data_classification.

Secrets
- All secrets must be stored in KMS-backed secret store (AWS Secrets Manager / HashiCorp Vault). No plaintext secrets in code or repo.

Networking
- Use explicit security groups and least-privilege IAM roles. Private endpoints for internal services.
- Subnets: separate control plane, data plane and management subnets with subnet-level routing policies.

CI/CD
- Build artifacts are immutable: tag with semantic version + build SHA.
- Canary policy: default 5% traffic for 15 minutes before full rollout unless SLO-sensitive (then use staged rollout with verification).
- Rollbacks must be automated on health-check failures.

4) MODEL-SERVING STANDARDS

Model packaging
- Serve models as versioned artifacts with manifest.yaml including required metadata: architecture, tokenizer, tokenizer_version, quantization_profile, input_schema, max_sequence_length. Example manifest snippet:

  architecture: gpt-neox
  model_version: v1.3.0
  quantization_profile: q4_0
  max_sequence_length: 2048

Quantization & compatibility
- Approved quantization profiles are maintained in /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles. Profiles must include expected quality deltas and recommended fallback variants.

Model config (example)
- Each deployment requires a model_config.yaml with: concurrency_limit, max_initial_tokens, kv_cache_sharing (true/false), batching_policy, timeout_ms. Table view (as CSV-like lines in this doc):

  field,description,example
  concurrency_limit,max concurrent inferences per replica,8
  batching_policy,min_batch_size: 1,max_batch_size: 32, min_latency_ms: 5

Rollout & compatibility
- Canary policy for model changes: 1) deploy variant with 1 replica in canary, 2) route 1% traffic for 30 minutes with automatic quality checks (eval prompts), 3) increase to 10% for 2 hours, 4) full rollout if no regressions.
- Incompatibility matrix: list expected breaking changes (tokenizer changes, context-window changes). If manifest indicates breaking change, require opt-in upgrade via canary.

Model observability
- Emit per-request metadata: model_id, model_version, quant_profile, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, prompt_quality_score (when available).

5) OBSERVABILITY STANDARDS

Metrics (naming conventions)
- Use Prometheus-style metrics: <service>_<resource>_<metric> (e.g., serving_inference_latency_ms_bucket).
- Required metrics for services handling inference:
  - inference_requests_total (labels: model_id, route, status)
  - inference_latency_ms_bucket (histogram)
  - inference_tokens_consumed_total
  - model_cache_hit_total

Traces
- Instrument entry and exit points with tracing. Use OpenTelemetry semantic conventions. Span names must include route + model_id when relevant.

Logs
- Structured JSON logs with fields: timestamp, level, service, trace_id, span_id, request_id, message, extra. Avoid PII/token content in logs.

SLOs & Alerts
- Default SLOs for user-facing inference endpoints: 95th percentile latency < 200ms for short-form models, < 800ms for long-context jobs; availability 99.9% monthly.
- Alert types: latency_sla_breach, error_rate_increase (>0.5% over baseline 10m), request_queue_growth, model_regression_detected.
- Alert priorities and runbooks are stored in eng-platform/runbooks.

Dashboards
- Dashboards per-route and per-model with: request rate, error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, model_quality_over_time.

6) PERFORMANCE STANDARDS & BENCHMARKING

Latency and throughput
- Define per-model performance targets in the model manifest and in the model catalog. Example targets:
  - small-embedder: p95 latency < 25ms @ 128-QPS
  - long-context-35b: p95 latency < 450ms @ 8-QPS

Benchmarking process
1. Reproducible harness: use eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite. Benchmarks must include: input distribution, prompt templates, token distributions, and concurrency patterns.
2. Baseline runs: cold-start, warm-start with KV cache primed, and sustained load.
3. Report: include p50/p95/p99, throughput at target latency, GPU utilization, memory, and kernel-level counters when available.

Profiling & Optimization
- Use tracing + GPU profiler for root-cause. Maintain a short list of regression indicators (increased KV miss rate, batch size drop, oscillating GC).

Caching & Batching guidance
- Prefer prefix caching for conversational workloads. Enable continuous batching for short requests but enforce per-customer latency SLOs.

7) ADOPTION, ADRS & CHANGE PROCESS

ADR index (recent notable decisions)
- ADR-2025-11: Default to gRPC for internal high-throughput RPCs (date: 2025-11-02, owners: Marco Diaz)
- ADR-2025-02: Standardize on q4_0 and q8_0 quantization profiles for production (date: 2025-02-14, owners: Priya Nair)
- ADR-2026-01: Introduced per-route SLO budgeting and cost-aware routing policy (date: 2026-01-12, owners: Andre Gomez)

How to propose a change (standards or ADR)
1. Create an ADR draft in the architecture-and-standards/decision-records directory with: context, alternatives considered, decision, consequences, and migration plan.
2. Seek reviewers: owner_team + infra + platform + one cross-functional reviewer.
3. After approval, publish to Confluence and tag related repos.

Exceptions & temporary measures
- Exceptions require a written mitigation plan and expiration date. Submit exception request to eng-standards@redwood.com.

8) OWNERSHIP & REVIEW CADENCE

- Standards Owner: Architecture & Standards Guild (rotating chair). Primary contact: architecture-standards@redwood.com.
- Review cadence: quarterly review of standards and after any major incident.
- Decommissioning: standards older than 36 months must be revalidated or archived.

Appendices

A. Example model_config.yaml

  # model_config.yaml example
  model_id: gpt-neox-1.3b
  model_version: v1.3.0
  concurrency_limit: 8
  batching_policy:
    min_batch: 1
    max_batch: 32
    max_wait_ms: 10
  kv_cache_sharing: true
  timeout_ms: 60000

B. API design checklist (for PRs)
- Does the API include versioning?
- Are pagination and rate limits defined?
- Is the auth method documented?
- Are error codes stable and enumerated?
- Are contract tests added?

C. ADR template (short)
- Title:
- Date:
- Status: proposed|accepted|deprecated
- Context:
- Decision:
- Consequences: migration steps or compatibility notes

References
- See also: confluence/architecture-and-standards/architecture-and-standards-guidelines-2026
- Model quantization profiles: confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles
- Runtime benchmarking: confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite

Contact
- Architecture & Standards Guild: architecture-standards@redwood.com
